scope: External-source static unitary-prefix compiler comparison. Sources are established community benchmark suites, not an accreditation standard. Benchpress is a methodology reference, not executed as a suite.

sources.name: QASMBench
sources.title: QASMBench: A Low-level QASM Benchmark Suite for NISQ Evaluation and Simulation
sources.license: Upstream Battelle license retained verbatim; see external_sources/qasmbench/LICENSE and NOTICE
sources.role: Raw non-transpiled OpenQASM2 source in small/medium directories, deterministic resource and static-unitary eligibility rule.

sources.name: MQT Bench
sources.title: MQT Bench: Benchmarking Software and Design Automation Tools for Quantum Computing
sources.role: Algorithm-level generators with bound parameters using the upstream seed10. No target-independent/native/mapped optimization is used. Original generated circuits retained as QPY.

sources.name: Benchpress
sources.title: Benchmarking the performance of quantum computing software for quantum circuit creation, manipulation and compilation
sources.role: Methodological precedent for common workloads, separate loading/compilation costs, two-qubit count/depth, multiple target graphs, and reporting unsupported/error/timeout cases. No claim that this study reproduces Benchpress settings or executes its full test suite.

selection_rule.eligibility: static unitary circuit after only global terminal-measurement suffix and barrier removal

normalization.track: Common static gate input; not a source-preserving native API comparison. Gate definitions and whole-circuit global phase convention are recorded per circuit.
normalization.terminal_measurements: Only a global suffix of measurements is removed; gates after the first measurement, resets and classical control are excluded. Barriers are removed and counted.
normalization.source_definitions: QASMBench uses its exact pinned qelib1.inc, inlined before import. Named primitives are retained only after checking the complete operation matrix against analytic gates, including controlled operations. Other operations use source/Qiskit definitions; Qiskit may internally synthesize those definitions. Permutations expand exactly into SWAPs. No compiler optimization, layout or routing is invoked.
normalization.source_reference: Qiskit Statevector on original generated/imported unitary prefix versus independent NumPy analytic gate simulator on canonical and normalized forms. Shared parser/generator trust boundary remains.
